newsitem.title: USA: Virginia municipalities raise tax cut concerns.
newsitem.headline: Virginia municipalities raise tax cut concerns.

text.p: Virginia municipal leaders have sent a letter urging Gov. George Allen to weigh the effect on services as he studies a $2.1 billion tax cut proposal, Richmond Times-Dispatch reported.
The governor has appointed a bipartisan commission to study reviving the proposed cuts, which he sought unsuccessfully in the last legislative session.

In a letter to Allen, the presidents of Virginia Municipal League and Virginia Association of Counties wrote, "It is easy to suggest cutting taxes; however it would be irresponsible to ignore the consequenses ... But the current reality is that most tax cuts would necessarily result in cuts to basic services."
In a reply late last week, Allen said, "The issues you raised...are important considerations that I am sure will be a part of the commission's discussions."
He said the tax study commission had no preconceived views and would not simply serve as a rubber stamp for Allen's proposal. The commission held its first meeting in July.

The newspaper described the municipal officials' letter as an early and bipartisan broadside against the Republican governor's effort to jump-start a tax cut in time for the 1997 gubernatorial and legislative elections.
